name: ESSAI 2026
venue: European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence, Vienna, Austria
description: The 2026 European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence (ESSAI) will be held in Vienna, Austria, bringing together PhD students and young researchers working on all aspects of AI. The program offers a one‑week intensive schedule of introductory and advanced courses, specialized tutorials on Bilateral AI and Digital Humanism, and a rich social programme including a reception at the Vienna City Hall. Co‑located with the 5th ACM Europe Digital Humanism Summer School, ESSAI provides extensive networking opportunities with over 30 lecturers and international experts.

name: OpenEuroLLM Winter School
venue: Skeikampen conference hotel, near Oslo, Norway
description: The 2026 Winter School on Multilinguality in LLM Development and Evaluation is organized by the Nordic Language Processing Laboratory and held at the Skeikampen conference hotel north of Oslo, Norway. It targets NLP researchers, especially those from EuroHPC consortium countries and doctoral students, offering technical presentations, hands‑on elements, and discussions on multilingual large language models and evaluation methods. The program includes expert talks, a walk‑through of EuroHPC experience reports, and networking opportunities, with subsidized participation and free bus transfer from Oslo Airport.

name: Probabilistic AI School
description: ProbAI School 2026 is a Probabilistic AI School taking place in Vilnius, Lithuania. The school aims to provide an inclusive educational environment covering state‑of‑the‑art machine learning and artificial intelligence topics. It welcomes enthusiasts, students, academics, and industry professionals to participate in the program.

name: BMVA Computer Vision Summer School
description: The 29th BMVA Computer Vision Summer School will be held at Durham University in Durham, England, UK. It offers an intensive week of lectures and lab sessions covering a wide range of topics in computer vision, delivered by leading researchers from the UK and abroad. The programme features daily oral talks and hands‑on sessions designed for students and early‑career researchers seeking advanced training in the field.

name: Oxford Machine Learning Summer School 2026
venue: Oxford Machine Learning School, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: The Oxford ML School (OxML) 2026 offered three advanced machine‑learning programmes in a mix of online and hybrid formats. The curriculum covered practical AI model building, health‑ and bio‑informatics applications, and the latest advances in representation learning and generative AI. The school brought together researchers and practitioners from around the world to train participants in cutting‑edge ML techniques.

name: Robotics, Perception and Learning (RPL) Summer School
venue: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden
description: The RPL Summer School 2026, organized by the Department for Robotics, Perception and Learning at KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm, Sweden, targets doctoral and postdoctoral researchers. It covers a broad spectrum of topics such as machine learning, computer vision, robotics, human‑robot interaction, planning and decision making, combining keynote talks, industry panels, and brainstorming sessions to foster new collaborations. The six‑day event takes place at the Happy Tammsvik resort, where participants receive fully funded accommodation, meals, and activities, and aim to leave with concrete research leads.

name: Machine Learning Crash Course at MALGA
description: The MLCC2026 Summer School – Machine Learning Crash Course – provides an introduction to fundamental machine‑learning concepts and algorithms. It is aimed at undergraduate and graduate students, as well as professionals, and is open to participants from any university after a selection process. The five‑day in‑person program in Genoa combines theoretical lectures with hands‑on lab sessions and includes a final test consisting of notebook work and a report.

name: UK Robotics Summer School
venue: National Robotarium, Heriot-Watt University, Edinburgh, United Kingdom
description: The UK Robotics Summer School 2026 is a five‑day program held in Edinburgh that brings together master’s‑level students and industry practitioners to explore robotics. It offers expert‑led lectures, tutorials and industry talks covering bio‑inspired robotics, healthcare robotics, generative AI, safe AI and real‑world applications, with hands‑on experience using state‑of‑the‑art technology. Participants also benefit from networking opportunities and a special summer school dinner.

name: International Summer School for Advanced Studies on Biometrics, Behavior, and Vision
description: The 2026 Biometrics Summer School takes place in Alghero, Sardinia, Italy, hosted at the Hotel Dei Pini. It focuses on the impact of generative AI and large foundation models on biometric and human‑recognition technologies, covering machine learning, image understanding, signal analysis, neuroscience, robotics, forensic and digital forensics. The program is aimed at PhD students, post‑docs, researchers and professionals such as forensic examiners and police officers, offering intensive lectures by leading experts, hands‑on sessions, and optional scholarships.

name: Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal (ELS) aspects of AI and AS at Umeå University
description: The Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal aspects of AI and Autonomous Systems is held at Umeå University in Sweden. It offers lectures, hands‑on multidisciplinary training, a poster session and a social program aimed at researchers and practitioners interested in the societal implications of AI and AS. The three‑day event (11–13 March 2026) provides networking opportunities and practical experience in ethical, legal and societal challenges of emerging technologies.

name: Winter School on Social Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia (SoRAIM 2026)
description: The ACM Europe Winter School on Social Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia (SoRAIM’27) will be held from 1 to 5 February 2027 in the Vercors mountains near Grenoble. It targets PhD students and early‑career researchers, offering lectures, hands‑on sessions and informal networking on topics such as computer vision, speech processing, affective computing and human‑robot interaction. The mountain setting provides opportunities for outdoor activities and fosters cross‑disciplinary collaboration among academia and industry participants.

name: Northern Lights Deep Learning Winter School
venue: UiT The Arctic University of Norway, Tromsø, Norway
description: The 2027 Northern Lights Deep Learning Winter School is part of the NLDL conference in Tromsø, Norway. It runs from 11 to 15 January 2027 and focuses on deep learning topics such as image classification, object detection, segmentation, time‑series prediction and speech recognition. The school brings together national and international researchers for hands‑on learning and networking at UiT The Arctic University of Norway.

name: Annual Nepal AI School (ANAIS)
description: The 7th Annual Nepal AI School (ANAIS) is an intensive 11‑day program offering AI lectures, labs, and project work in Kathmandu, Nepal. It targets senior undergraduates, graduate students, PhD candidates, faculty, and industry professionals, covering themes such as Geometric Deep Learning, World Models, Generative Modeling, and Neuro‑symbolic AI. The school aims to bring together over 500 in‑person participants and thousands of online viewers to foster collaboration and advance AI research in South Asia.

name: EEML Summer School
description: The Eastern European Machine Learning Summer School takes place in Cetinje, Montenegro from 27 July to 1 August 2026. It offers a series of lectures and tutorials delivered by leading experts from institutions such as Google DeepMind, MIT, and the University of Montenegro, covering topics in machine learning and artificial intelligence. The program is aimed at graduate students and early‑career researchers from the region who seek intensive training and networking opportunities.

name: Mediterranean Summer School
description: The Mediterranean Machine Learning (M2L) Summer School is a five‑day intensive program offering keynotes, lectures and hands‑on sessions led by international AI experts. It targets doctoral and outstanding master students, as well as academics and practitioners, focusing on topics such as computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, reinforcement learning and ethics in machine learning. The school emphasizes diversity, networking and knowledge transfer, providing opportunities for poster presentations, scholarships and cultural activities.

name: Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI
venue: Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications, Rabat, Morocco
description: The 2nd edition of the AI Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI is a five‑day immersive program jointly organized by MoroccoAI, INPT, IMT Nord Europe, and Soft Centre in Rabat, Morocco. It targets master and Ph.D. students, post‑docs, young and senior researchers, and professionals, offering expert lectures, hands‑on labs, and networking opportunities to build the next generation of AI leaders in the region. Participants will receive a clear overview of state‑of‑the‑art research, practical implementation experience, and access to a strong network of AI enthusiasts across Morocco.

name: AthNLP Summer School 2026
description: The Athens Natural Language Processing Summer School 2026 (AthNLP) is a week‑long program held at the NCSR Demokritos campus in Athens, Greece. It brings together experts from RC Athena, NCSR Demokritos, Athens University of Economics and Business, Heriot‑Watt University, Archimedes Unit/Athena RC, and ELLIS‑University of Manchester to deliver intensive lectures and hands‑on workshops on NLP research and applications. The school also supports the 14th EETN Conference on Artificial Intelligence, providing participants with networking opportunities and exposure to cutting‑edge AI developments.

name: Advanced Artificial Intelligence: GenAI & Deep Unsupervised Learning
venue: Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: The Advanced Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning summer school at Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, focuses on generative AI and deep unsupervised learning techniques. It offers theoretical lectures and hands‑on projects covering clustering, GANs, self‑supervised learning, anomaly detection and unsupervised reinforcement learning, with an emphasis on real‑world applications. The programme is aimed at STEM students with intermediate AI/ML experience who are considering graduate study or research.

name: AI4Science Summer School
description: The 2nd Summer School on Advancing Scientific Discovery with AI brings together researchers, PhD students and post‑doctoral scholars to explore how artificial intelligence can accelerate scientific research. The program covers machine‑learning for data analysis, AI‑driven experimental design, generative models, and integration of AI with physical simulations, and includes hands‑on workshops using Python libraries such as NumPy and PyTorch. Held in Caen, Normandy, France, the school aims to equip participants with practical skills for applying deep‑learning techniques to scientific problems.

name: LUT Summer School
description: LUT Summer School is a one‑week intensive program on the Lappeenranta campus offering courses on sustainability, climate action, marketing, management, and the intersection of business and technology. It is aimed at bachelor’s and master’s students who can earn 3 ECTS credits per course through lectures, workshops, group work and a social programme set in the Finnish summer environment. The programme combines academic learning with extracurricular activities such as sauna evenings, outdoor excursions, and networking opportunities.

name: 1st Internationa School on the Cognitive, Ethical, and Societal Dimensions of AI - AIces
description: AIces 2026 is the first International School on the Cognitive, Ethical and Societal Dimensions of Artificial Intelligence, targeting graduate students, postgraduate students and industry practitioners. The four‑day event in Porto offers parallel courses, a symposium for short presentations, and open‑debate sessions, with both face‑to‑face and live‑online participation options. Participants receive a certificate of attendance and can access recorded lectures for 45 days after the school.
